previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, GERD, and tobacco use was admitted for evaluation of positional chest pressure and shortness of breath that worsened when lying down. Initial concerns included cardiac ischemia, but serial troponins were negative, EKG showed no acute changes, and a stress test revealed no ischemic ST changes, making acute coronary syndrome unlikely. A chest X-ray was normal, and D-dimer was negative, ruling out pulmonary embolism. Symptoms improved with albuterol nebulizers, suggesting bronchospasm, and mildly elevated inflammatory markers along with a recent upper respiratory infection raised suspicion for viral pericarditis. She was treated with colchicine and discharged with an albuterol inhaler for symptom management. Her home medications were resumed, and she was advised to follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing evaluation.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Evaluation of the patient with chest tightness and shortness of
breath.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from outside hospital from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet
to the base of the lungs prior to administration of IV contrast.  Following
the administration of 100 cc of Optiray nonionic intravenous contrast,
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet to the base
of the lungs as per chest CTA protocol.  Multiplanar reformatted images were
prepared.

CHEST CTA:

Opacification of the pulmonary vasculature demonstrates no filling defects to
suggest a pulmonary embolus.  The aorta and great vessels are within normal
limits.  Of incidental note is the presence of a common origin of the left
subclavian and carotid arteries (bovine arch).  The heart is within normal
limits.

The airways are patent to subsegmental levels and the lungs are clear with no
evidence of consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax.  Two tiny 3-mm nodules
are visualized within the right middle lobe (3:27,33).

There is no hilar, mediastinal, or axillary lymphadenopathy.  A small hiatal
hernia is visualized.  This study is not tailored for evaluation of
subdiaphragmatic structures and the visualized portions of the liver, spleen,
stomach were normal.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions. 
Changes consistent with diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis are
visualized throughout the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic dissection.
2.  Two tiny 3-mm nodules are visualized in the right middle lobe.  If the
patient has no risk factors for lung cancer, no followup is needed.  If the
patient has risk factors for lung cancer, a followup chest CT in 12 months is
recommended.

INDICATION:  Recent fall, head trauma.

COMPARISON:  CT head on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
contrast was administered.  Bone algorithms obtained.  Coronal and sagittal
reformations were performed.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
infarction.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and configuration. 
There is no shift of normally midline structures.  The gray-white
differentiation is normal.  No fractures are identified.  The visualized
paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are well
aerated.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial pathologic process.  No hemorrhage.  No
fractures.
